edits.hypothesis: Explicit, task-agnostic guidance on output format (follow task specs exactly, avoid markdown, do not add extra information on the answer line) and systematic problem-solving approach will increase the likelihood that the model produces correctly formatted answers that extraction can identify and grade
edits.targets_mode: output_format_non_compliance; the model needs clear instruction on what 'follow the format exactly' means in practice
edits.why_not_lower_lever: This is instructional content about expectations and general problem-solving strategy. Prose is the appropriate lever for teaching the model what correct formatting and compliance looks like across diverse task types.
edits.trigger_condition: Always; applies to every task in every family
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) With explicit framing 'if task says "Answer with the name only", output ONLY the name', the model is more likely to honor format specs rather than add helpful-seeming context; (preservative) guidance reinforces systematic constraint-satisfaction reasoning (identify key constraints, enumerate scenarios) shown in evolve-logic-006 success; (transfer) format compliance and problem-solving structure are general and apply equally to logic, ledger, scheduling, text transformation, and other task families
edits.regression_risk: Low; guidance is additive and general, not overriding reasoning approaches or task-specific constraints
edits.mechanism: Explicit, task-agnostic guidance on output format (follow task specs exactly, avoid markdown, do not add extra information on the answer line) and systematic problem-solving approach will increase the likelihood that the model produces correctly formatted answers that extraction can identify and grade

edits.hypothesis: Implementing extraction logic that detects 'ANSWER:' prefix and extracts markdown-wrapped content at the start of the last line (**text** → text) will recover the correct answer even when the model outputs explanation or formatting, enabling accurate grading
edits.targets_mode: output_format_non_compliance; defensive extraction to handle model output that includes formatting or explanation despite instruction
edits.why_not_lower_lever: Prompt instruction cannot guarantee the model will never wrap answers in markdown or add extra text. This is a defensive plumbing fix: if the model outputs '**Sawyer** owns the rabbit.', extraction logic isolates 'Sawyer' so grading succeeds. Answer parsing and cleanup are control_flow concerns (information routing, output transformation), not prompt concerns.
edits.trigger_condition: Always when last line contains markdown formatting or 'ANSWER:' prefix; extraction applies to every solve() call
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) evolve-logic-002 output '**Sawyer** owns the rabbit.' would match pattern ^\*\*(.+?)\*\*, extract group 1 as 'Sawyer', enabling exact-match grading to succeed; (preservative) evolve-logic-006 and tasks that output clean answers pass through unchanged (no markdown found, last_line returned as-is); (transfer) markdown removal and prefix extraction are format-agnostic and work on any task output without task-specific logic
edits.regression_risk: Minimal; extraction is defensive (cleans, never manufactures content). Clean output passes through untouched. Risk only if a legitimate answer contains literal markdown like 'Use **bold** in the answer', which is rare in exact-answer tasks.
edits.mechanism: Implementing extraction logic that detects 'ANSWER:' prefix and extracts markdown-wrapped content at the start of the last line (**text** → text) will recover the correct answer even when the model outputs explanation or formatting, enabling accurate grading
